expect:
Tarn Hows in the Lake District is suitable. Students may include:
• Tarn Hows attracts over 750,000 visitors a year, well above its quiet carrying capacity.
• Heavy footfall compacts soil along paths, killing grass and mosses; rain then washes loose soil away creating wide muddy scars on the fellside.
• Cars overflow car parks and verges turn to mud, while litter blows into the tarn affecting wildlife.
• Honeypot pressure inflates house prices in nearby Hawkshead, pricing out local first-time buyers.
• Local shops shift towards tourist gifts and away from everyday goods, reducing services for residents.

Mastering: developed explanation with multiple linked impacts and accurate located detail.
Secure: clear explanation with a named site and at least two impacts.
Developing: some impacts identified but place detail thin.
Emerging: generic comments on tourism damage with no named example.
[6 marks]
